newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent Group Three diesel prices firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent Group Three diesel prices firm.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent low sulphur diesel fuel prices firmed in the Group Three market on stronger differentials and rising futures prices, traders said.

A resurgence in agricultural demand as drier weather moved into the Midwest and expectations of continued strong demand as the harvest season shifts into high gear fueled the rising diesel differentials, traders said.
"By the end of the month, low sulphur diesel is going to explode," one trader in the region, which is centered in Kansas City, Mo., said.
Low sulphur diesel was bid 1.75 cent over the print for prompt deliveries and 1.25 cent over the print for later deliveries in Group Three, moving one cent a gallon higher in late trade on Thursday.
In Chicago, low sulphur diesel differentials remained 3.0/2.75 cents under NYMEX November heating oil futures for all October timings, traders said.
High sulphur diesel differentials were steady at 1.25/0.75 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three and eased to 6.0 cents under the print in Chicago.
Unleaded gasoline for prompt deliveries was talked 1.25/1.0 cents under NYMEX November unleaded in both markets, with later deliveries 1.50/1.25 cents under the print.
